transcript:
[doctor] Hello there, how are you doing today?

[patient] Hi, Doctor. I'm feeling pretty tired, to be honest.

[doctor] I'm sorry to hear that. I see you're here because of some episodes of syncope and collapse. Can you tell me more about what happened?

[patient] Sure. I've had two severe episodes of fainting where I completely lost consciousness. The first one was about two weeks ago, and the second one happened six days ago.

[doctor] That sounds concerning. Did you notice any symptoms before you fainted, like dizziness or lightheadedness?

[patient] Yes, I felt really weak and fatigued before both episodes. But I didn't have any chest pain or palpitations.

[doctor] Hmm, I see. Did these episodes affect your daily activities in any way?

[patient] Definitely. I haven't been able to drive, and I had to miss work because of it.

[doctor] That must be tough. Have you experienced any fever, chills, or unexplained weight loss recently?

[patient] No, none of those.

[doctor] How about your heart? Any chest pain or palpitations outside of these episodes?

[patient] No, I haven't had any chest pain or palpitations.

[doctor] Alright. Have you noticed any other symptoms, like neurological issues or focal deficits?

[patient] No, just the fainting episodes.

[doctor] How are you sleeping these days?

[patient] Not great. I get about 5-6 hours of sleep, but it's often interrupted.

[doctor] And what about your diet? What do you usually eat?

[patient] My diet is mostly high in carbohydrates, but low in protein.

[doctor] Do you exercise regularly?

[patient] Not really. I rarely exercise.

[doctor] Do you smoke or use any tobacco products?

[patient] No, I don't.

[doctor] How about alcohol or drug use?

[patient] I don't use drugs, and I only drink socially, maybe 1-2 glasses of wine on weekends.

[doctor] Thanks for sharing that. Let's take a look at your vital signs. Your blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg when sitting and 90/60 mmHg when standing. Your heart rate is 72 bpm, respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, and your temperature is 98.7°F. Oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] On physical examination, you appear alert and in no acute distress. Your cardiovascular exam shows no murmurs, rubs, or gallops, but you do have orthostatic hypotension. Neurologically, you seem intact with no focal deficits, and cranial nerves II-XII are grossly intact. Musculoskeletal exam shows normal muscle strength and tone with no tenderness or deformities. Your lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with no wheezes, rales, or rhonchi.

[patient] Alright.

[doctor] We're still waiting for the results of your MRI of the brain, as well as blood work for thyroid function tests and serum electrolytes.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] Based on what we know, it seems like your syncope and collapse could be due to orthostatic hypotension. We also need to rule out other potential causes like neurocardiogenic syncope, hypoglycemia, cardiac arrhythmias, and neurological disorders.

[patient] That makes sense.

[doctor] I'm going to start you on Midodrine, 5 mg, one tablet three times daily by mouth. It's important to increase your fluid intake and avoid standing for long periods. Also, try to rise slowly from sitting or lying positions and consider wearing compression stockings.

[patient] Got it.

[doctor] We will also proceed with the MRI of the brain to rule out any neurological causes and continue with the blood work to evaluate underlying causes.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] I'm referring you to a neurologist for further evaluation. I've scheduled an appointment with Dr. Emily Brown.

[patient] Alright.

[doctor] Please follow up with me in one week to review the MRI and blood work results, reassess your symptoms, and adjust the treatment plan as necessary.

[patient] Sure, I'll do that.

[doctor] Just to make sure you understand, it's important to adhere to the medication despite your busy work schedule. Midodrine can have side effects, so keep an eye out for any new symptoms and let us know immediately if you notice anything unusual.

[patient] Will do.

[doctor] Regarding your diet, try to focus on balanced nutrition with adequate protein intake. Gradually increase your physical activity as tolerated.

[patient] Alright, I'll work on that.

[doctor] Do you have any questions or concerns about the plan we've discussed?

[patient] No, I think that's everything for now.

[doctor] Great. If anything comes up or you have any questions later, don't hesitate to reach out. Take care and I'll see you at the follow-up.

[patient] Thank you, Doctor. I'll see you then.
